content: How much compute did you guys utilize?

Hi everyone! While we wait for the ratings to settle, here's a brief overview of our approach.

At different points during the competition, we reached #1 with agents from both our 10M- and 20M-parameter model lines, as well as with our standalone heuristic planner. We explored both training on more games and increasing model capacity. Ultimately, we chose a 10M model with a rule-based action patch at inference time.

The three figures below illustrate how we got there:

  1. Training loop We alternated behavior cloning (BC) with self-play PPO, learning from public replays and demonstrations generated by our heuristic planner. Replay analysis helped us identify weaknesses in the learned policy, improve the planner, and generate targeted demonstrations for the next training cycle.

  2. Training history This figure traces the repeated BC/PPO stages, the introduction of heuristic-generated demonstrations, and the parallel 10M and 20M model lines. The final 10M model's training lineage includes approximately 8.29 million self-play games.

  3. Architecture and inference A shared Transformer predicts unit actions and market orders. Our chosen configuration, Final A, applies a rule-based action patch to resolve conflicts, avoid wasteful actions, and manage inventory. The figure also includes Final B, a variant trained with rule-aware PPO and sequential action masks.

Our code is available on GitHub.

Team contributions:

  • morim3: Neural network architecture and the 10M model line, testing the hypothesis that more self-play games lead to stronger agents.
  • msd0110: The 20M model line, testing the hypothesis that more parameters lead to stronger agents.
  • Piiiiiiiii: Development of a strong heuristic planner.
  • qistripute: Rule-based action patches and replay analysis, identifying weaknesses in our evolving strategies and suggesting improvements.

We'll publish a detailed writeup once the ratings have converged and the final standings are confirmed.

Thanks to everyone who tilled the fields alongside us!
A surprising solution—thanks for sharing, and congratulations!

Congrats! Really impressive results. Did you find much difference in 10M vs 20M parameters? (I imagine it was somewhat confounded by other architecture changes).

My model ended up being just under 1M parameters, same self-play and BC ideas but no heuristics.
amazing work! thanks for sharing your approch!

Hello, thank you for the write-up and open sourcing the repo.

May I ask you a question as someone new to reinforcement learning?

I also tried RL with initial BC + self-play. At some point during self-play, I did BC again, but the model quality dropped (it lost too many games against the checkpoint before the second BC), so I discarded that second BC checkpoint and went back to self-play.

Is this kind of quality drop normal? I wonder I should have kept that second BC checkpoint and continued self-play from there.

I had a similar experience. After running BC again on my PPO-trained model, the resulting checkpoint lost all 100 games against the checkpoint from before the second BC. However, when I resumed PPO self-play from that second BC checkpoint, it became stronger than the pre-BC checkpoint after about 60,000 games.

Ah, thank you. I really should have continued training after my second BC. May I also ask what kind of compute you had? I found in your repo that you used A100 and A30, but couldn't find the counts.

And congratulations 🥳

Thank you! My teammate used up to 17 A100s and 29 A30s for the 10M PPO run, averaging around 7 A100s and 20 A30s. For the 20M PPO run, I used up to 26 A100s. We’ll share more details in a write-up later!
